vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: improvement-executor
Version: 1.1.0

The improvement-executor skill bundle is a utility for applying and rolling back structured modifications to Markdown and YAML files. The scripts (execute.py and rollback.py) implement file editing actions such as section replacement and frontmatter updates, including mandatory backups and dry-run capabilities. The code uses safe practices like yaml.safe_load and path resolution, and there is no evidence of data exfiltration, malicious execution, or harmful prompt injection instructions.

llm.summary: The skill's code, CLI, and instructions are consistent with an executor that applies, backs up, and rolls back file-based improvements; it does modify files on disk but requests no unrelated credentials or network access.

dimensions.detail: Name/description match what the code implements: file-targeted actions (append/replace/insert/update YAML), automatic backups, and rollback. The scripts operate on a supplied ranking artifact / receipt and target paths, which is expected for an executor.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and the CLI map to the provided scripts. The runtime instructions and code read ranking/receipt JSON and then read/write files on disk (target_path, backup files, state under a state_root). This is in-scope for a file-modification executor, but it means the skill will overwrite user files specified in artifacts—use only with trusted ranking/receipt inputs and prefer --dry-run first.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec; code files are included. There is no network download or package install, so nothing extra is pulled in at install time.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required env vars or secrets. The rollback script does consult OPENCLAW_ROOT if set (defaulting to ~/.openclaw/shared-context/...), which is reasonable for locating receipts/backups but means it can access files under that path.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Skill is not always-enabled and does not request elevated platform privileges. It reads/writes files and updates its own state under a state_root (via lib.state_machine) which is expected for its purpose and does not modify other skills or system-wide agent configuration.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it says: modify markdown/YAML frontmatter and support backups/rollbacks. Before running it: 1) Always run in --dry-run first to preview changes. 2) Only feed it ranking.json / receipt artifacts you trust—it will read target_path values and can overwrite those files. 3) Be aware it will look under the OpenClaw shared context (OPENCLAW_ROOT or ~/.openclaw) for receipts/backups; review those files if you rely on implicit discovery. 4) PyYAML is optional; frontmatter updates will report an error if PyYAML is not installed. If you need stronger safety, run the scripts in an isolated workspace or review the specific ranking/receipt JSON contents before execution.
